Despite residual image-level errors, AI-derived target-occurrence rates closely reproduced expert-derived signals after aggregation (mean absolute error = 0.0432, Pearson $r$ = 0.9696, Spearman $\rho$ = 0.9568). Agreement remained strong across multi-session windows, and elevated, strong, and persistent occurrence proxies were recovered in held-out testing. These results show that AI-based phytoplankton classification can support monitoring-relevant temporal indicators beyond image-level identification and support future operational early-warning development.

title: VERDICT: Visual Extraction-Result Decoder with Integrated Confidence and Traceable Evidence
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Workshop on VLM4RWD
summary: Enterprises run schema-guided structured field extraction on documents with frontier multimodal models, and accuracy keeps improving as new models and systems arrive. Two things have not kept pace: the evidence for each extracted value, meaning the location of the document it was read from, and how far to trust the value and that evidence. Neither is a component of most extraction systems today, so we build them as a framework that attaches to an existing extractor and leaves it untouched. We present VERDICT, a plug-in framework that uses a small Vision--Language Model (VLM) to ground/localize the evidence once per document over a fixed external extractor's output, then calibrates value and evidence confidence. Fine-tuning the VLM for evidence localization substantially improves visual evidence quality and, more importantly, expands VERDICT's selective-prediction operating range. At a strict confidence threshold $0.80$, VERDICT with the fine-tuned VLM gives usable precision--coverage trade-offs for both value and evidence confidence across the in-distribution and out of distribution datasets, whereas the frozen setting often collapses to little or no coverage. Running an open-weight VLM for localization rather than a closed API makes its internal states available to the calibrator, and they are worth more than output log-probabilities: in-distribution AUROC rises from $0.730$ to $0.914$ for value confidence and from $0.681$ to $0.906$ for evidence confidence. This advantage does not survive a distribution shift. We show that the signal is displaced rather than destroyed, and that labeling roughly $120$ fields from the target dataset takes evidence confidence from $0.641$ to $0.905$ on one dataset and from $0.675$ to $0.829$ on the other.

title: Fast Construction of Inner Sphere Trees Using Machine Learning
summary: Collision detection for complex non-convex objects is a bottleneck in physics simulation, virtual reality, and robotics. Inner sphere trees (ISTs) answer proximity and penetration queries efficiently, but their greedy leaf-sphere construction is sequential and computationally expensive, which limits both large-scale preprocessing and runtime use. In this work, we present ML-IST, a machine-learning-based method that reformulates leaf-sphere generation as a single-shot set-prediction problem: a network predicts a fixed set of inscribed sphere candidates from multichannel voxel geometry, differentiable coverage feedback corrects the coarse prediction and fills residual gaps at finer scales, and a lightweight geometric projection enforces validity. Averaged over the test set, a single-GPU implementation of ML-IST reduces mean leaf-generation time by a factor of $2.0$--$2.6$ over single-core CPU construction across target capacities of 64--512 spheres, and qualitative results on complex models show multiscale sphere distributions that follow principal volumes and slender features. We further integrate ML-IST into the Jolt Physics and Bullet engines; in an alpha-puzzle benchmark it reaches 55.89~FPS, the highest among the compared representations (conventional IST, GImpact, and convex decomposition). These results support learned leaf generation as a practical component for fast, runtime construction of detailed collision representations.

title: ESCAPE: Egocentric Sensing for Collision Avoidance and Policy Execution
summary: Motion planning in unstructured environments is a bottleneck for robot deployment. Current visuomotor policies predominantly rely on external cameras, introducing perceptual blind spots and fragility due to occlusions, clutter, and calibration constraints. To overcome these limitations, we propose ESCAPE, an online egocentric sensing framework for collision-free trajectory generation. ESCAPE aggregates sparse measurements from distributed depth sensors, converting them into a structured, obstacle-aware point cloud representation. Our policy leverages a flow matching-based generative framework, and trains on a high-quality dataset comprising over 100K safety-critical trajectories. With joint optimization of goal-reaching and collision objectives, it produces safe trajectories directly from these egocentric inputs. Crucially, ESCAPE is trained entirely in simulation and transfers zero-shot to physical hardware without any real-world fine-tuning. Extensive simulation and real-world evaluations demonstrate that ESCAPE achieves stable motion planning using only egocentric perception, outperforming external-view and voxelized-planning baselines across both simulation and real-world evaluations.

title: CrowdH-Edit: Reference-Guided Instruction-Based Synthetic Hajj Crowd Image Generation for Crowd Counting
summary: The scarcity of domain-specific annotated images remains a major limitation for developing computer-vision systems for Hajj crowd analysis. Existing crowd-counting datasets and unconstrained generative models do not capture Hajj-specific visual conditions, including sacred-site geometry, white-clothed pilgrim crowds, and indoor/outdoor illumination variation. This study presents CrowdH-Edit, a reference-guided, instruction-based framework for synthetic Hajj crowd-image generation. Real Hajj images provide structural references, while textual instructions guide changes in crowd conditions and illumination and help preserve the main scene layout. Stable Diffusion 2.1 and Stable Diffusion XL 1.0 with low-rank adaptation were evaluated as comparative baselines. Qwen Image Edit was used without additional training within a ComfyUI workflow and selected for final dataset construction. The workflow produced CrowdH-Edit, a cleaned pool of 6,122 synthetic images, from which 387 images were selected and annotated to construct CrowdH-Edit-Ann-387. Among the evaluated generation pipelines, Qwen Image Edit achieved the highest semantic-alignment score and the lowest distributional and perceptual distances. Downstream evaluation across five crowd-counting models showed that adding the annotated synthetic subset to real training data reduced mean absolute error for three models and root mean squared error for two. These findings indicate that reference-guided synthetic Hajj imagery can support crowd-counting training, although its benefits depend on the model and evaluation metric.

title: DS-Net: A Dynamic Split Network for Edge-Cloud Collaborative Inference
comment: 18 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
summary: Collaborative inference serves as a critical methodology in edge intelligence. Existing collaborative inference methods operate by splitting the deep neural network (DNN) model between edge devices and cloud servers. However, these methods need to load different models for multiple split points when the communication or device changes, thus resulting in long switching times and substantial storage overhead on the edge side. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic Split Network (DS-Net), which not only enables efficient split point switching but also enhances the collaborative speed and accuracy across various scenarios. Specifically, we design a dynamic switching framework that enables flexible selection among multiple split points within a single model, thereby reducing storage, memory, and switching overhead. To mitigate the feature distribution shifts and task-relevant information loss caused by dynamic splitting and high-ratio compression, we further propose a hierarchical compensation mechanism. Local alignment calibrates the decoded feature distribution at each split point, while task-specific global compensation restores task-relevant information at the global level. In addition, we incorporate sample-adaptive global compensation selection into split-point selection based on sample complexity and runtime resource conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that DS-Net reduces memory overhead by 74.6% and achieves millisecond-level switching latency. Moreover, under a 10 Mbps bandwidth constraint on the Nano platform, DS-Net outperforms state-of-the-art collaborative methods by achieving 1.2% higher accuracy on the COCO dataset, reducing latency by 42.5%, and improving throughput by a factor of 1.8$\times$.

title: DISCERN: Identifiable Disease Evidence for Generalizable Medical Multimodal Learning
summary: Clinical multimodal models can learn enrollment shortcuts shared across modalities and fail on new cohorts. We model these data through a latent structural causal model: disease state and background factors generate physiology through shared mechanisms, while cohorts differ in selection and measurement. Holding acquisition fixed, we identify conditional disease evidence without observing disease-state labels or recovering the full causal model. In common Gaussian coordinates, cross-cohort state alignment and natural-parameter changes identify a minimal selection statistic; conditioning on it removes enrollment-dependent evidence and yields an identifiable reference posterior within the specified shift family. State-dependent interactions can carry evidence invisible to individual-modality posteriors, motivating joint, information-preserving representations. DISCERN combines an information-lattice encoder, a latent-state model, and an outcome head through joint training. Under reversed synthetic enrollment on known latent coordinates, conditioning raises state AUROC from 0.043 to 0.883 and from 0.265 to 0.825, while random conditioning does not. Exploratory cross-database mortality experiments between eICU and MIMIC-IV improve AUROC over matched empirical risk minimization by 0.036 and 0.035. Learned-coordinate diagnostics distinguish preservation of state information from identification of the coordinates required by the estimator.

title: Functionalizing AI-Generated 3D Shapes via Interior Geometry Construction
summary: AI-based 3D generation models such as Hunyuan 3D and Meshy can produce visually appealing 3D shapes from an image or text this http URL , they typically focus on an object's external appearance, often producing incomplete or implausible interior geometry. Consequently, the generated shapes are not guaranteed to be functionally valid, limiting their direct use in downstream applications such as simulation and fabrication. In this paper, we present a computational approach to functionalize AI-generated 3D shapes through interior geometry construction. Our key observations are that a part's functional role defines its interior geometry, and such geometry is often smooth, relatively simple, and closely related to the part's external shape. Inspired by these observations, we introduce an interior-aware part graph to encode information necessary for constructing interior geometry within an AI-generated 3D shape, and build the graph via VLM-based shape segmentation and graph attribute inference. Guided by the graph, we model the interior geometry of each part as a generalized cylinder and infer its parameters from the part's external geometry through an optimization. The resulting 3D shapes are functionally valid while preserving their AI-generated external appearance. We demonstrate our approach on a variety of AI-generated 3D shapes, including vessels, containers, and storage furniture, and fabricate selected examples for functional validation.

title: Same Space or Not: Benchmarking Spatial Intelligence Through Cross-View Contradictions
summary: Spatial intelligence, the capacity to represent and reason about physical space, underlies embodied perception and real-world visual understanding. Existing benchmarks probe it through spatial relations, perspective-taking, and mental modeling. What remains underexamined is whether a model can maintain a coherent scene representation across views, since pairwise comparison alone cannot reveal which view departs from the truth. We thus introduce Same Space or Not (SSoN), a benchmark of cross-view contradiction resolution comprising 1,000 questions from seven indoor scene sources and six categories of controlled 3D edits. Each question presents three views of an unchanged scene and one view of an edited variant. Models must identify the inconsistent view and explain the contradiction without a designated trusted reference or a marked target. Our pipeline iteratively translates human review into generation constraints. Automated checks and exhaustive human validation screen out both trivial visual shortcuts and questions lacking sufficient evidence for a unique answer. Humans achieve 83.3% accuracy, compared with 39.7% for the strongest vision-language models (VLMs), falling to 34.9% when a valid visual explanation is also required. We investigate prompting, camera information, and 3D reconstruction as interventions. On a 100-question intervention set with a 24% baseline, prompting and 3D reconstruction remain below 50% answer accuracy, except when ground-truth camera information is supplied, which reaches 61% answer accuracy but only 48% True solve accuracy. On a held-out 201-question test set, Qwen2.5-VL-7B achieves 21.89% accuracy, 33.33% after answer-only fine-tuning, and 41.79% after fine-tuning on both rationales and answers. These results identify cross-view contradiction resolution as a substantial weakness of current VLMs that can be partly addressed by targeted supervision.

title: A Configurable ETC2 Encoder with Learned Search
summary: ETC2 fixes the texture representation and bit rate, leaving the encoder to trade search time for distortion. We present a configurable CPU encoder in which rules or small neural networks allocate conventional ETC2 searches; these searches construct every encoded block. Configurations span fast-encoder output through broader mode and endpoint searches. On 64 color textures used to evaluate and select configurations, the fastest measured configurations reaching at least Google Etc2Comp's pooled REC709 PSNR at efforts 0-49.5 run 30.7-40.9 times faster. A high-quality configuration exceeds effort-100 PSNR with 64.1% less time. At equal search quotas, learned action ranking and second-search allocation jointly gain 0.124 dB over rule-based choices. At high quality, learning saves time at a small distortion cost. Outputs retain standard ETC2 storage and hardware decoding.

title: Generalizable fetal brain biometry via adaptive artificial intelligence
summary: Reliable fetal brain biometry on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosing congenital brain anomalies, but artificial intelligence models often lose accuracy under domain shifts. We developed BioTTA, a backbone-agnostic, source-free unsupervised test-time adaptation framework that adapts pretrained models online to individual unlabeled target volumes. This retrospective multicohort study included 394 reconstructed 3D fetal brain MRI volumes at 20-39 gestational weeks, with 11 biometric measurements annotated by radiologists. BioTTA was developed on single-center turbo spin-echo MRI and evaluated on three datasets representing cross-sequence, cross-center, and cross-nation shifts. Biometry accuracy was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and the percentage of correct measurements within 4 mm. A web-based reporting platform mapped measurements onto normative growth trajectories and was evaluated against radiologists in four multicenter disease cohorts covering germinal matrix-intraventricular hemorrhage, ventriculomegaly, and cerebellar abnormality. Across all three target datasets, BioTTA outperformed auto-SVRTK, source-only models, and FetalSynthGen, while matching models finetuned with target labels. MAEs ranged from 1.10 to 1.46 mm with a convolutional backbone and from 1.46 to 2.25 mm with a transformer backbone. Diagnostic accuracy ranged from 82.1% to 95.0%, comparable to a senior radiologist. BioTTA supports accurate, generalizable fetal brain biometry and standardized prenatal brain growth assessment across heterogeneous MRI sources.

title: Geo-vision: Native-Resolution Geometry and Sampled Topology for Vehicle-Part Damage Classification
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. Code: this https URL
summary: Geo-vision classifies vehicle-part damage using a fixed representation combining appearance, multiscale geometry, orientation, and sampled digital topology. Connected components, holes, Euler characteristics, and spatial arrangement complement amplitude-sensitive pooling and a supervised tree classifier. We establish amplitude preservation, axial sign invariance, and conditional operator stability. Retrospective checkpoint evaluation on 55,303 crops from 4,916 source groups yields average precision 0.7577, exceeding 0.7458 for an ImageNet-pretrained frozen YOLO11n comparator on identical crops. The complete added structural block, comprising topology, occupancy, and component location, improves average precision by 0.00493 beyond appearance and geometry. Geo-vision uses no external encoder pretraining and has higher AP point estimates at every matched label budget. With approximately 25% fewer task labels, its AP point estimate exceeds full-data YOLO, although the adjusted interval includes zero. Complete serial CPU inference requires 26.98 ms per crop versus YOLO's 11.20 ms, with peak memory 185 versus 437 MiB. Independent external validation remains necessary.

title: IMPULSE: Push First, Then Predict in V-JEPA 2 Feature Space
summary: Latent world models such as V-JEPA 2 forecast in the feature space of a video encoder, but one look at an object does not reveal how hard it is to rotate, how much it bounces or how much it slides. People find out by trying: a few pokes reveal how an object responds. IMPULSE, named after the impulse response it infers, gives a predictor in frozen V-JEPA 2 feature space the same ability. A Bayesian contact memory summarizes three short calibration pushes, a predicted object pose carries it into the predictor, and a lightweight random-Fourier pose head lets the predictor use the pose. On 512 fresh objects, in a pre-specified held-out confirmation with models sealed before the data existed, the memory lowers the 1-second feature-forecast error by 11.6-12.8% relative to the same predictor without experience, for all 8 training seeds, with a 95% seed-and-object interval excluding zero. The gain also holds for 128 objects with out-of-range physics (11.7-14.0%), and the full extension beats a plain predictor by 15.5-16.6%. An information-ladder argument, exact for ideal predictors, shows that physics reaches the features only through motion, so we measure how much the pathway lets pose help. On fresh objects, the Fourier head roughly triples the gain of a perfect memory over plain pose tokens (2.8-3.2x). Raw push measurements fed through the same pathway give a similar gain, so the Bayesian summary is not required; it condenses the trials into eight interpretable numbers. The gain is absent at contact onset and grows afterwards.

title: Learning When to Trust and Reobserve Sparse-Frame VideoQA from Temporal Sampling Perturbations
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Physical Understanding for Decision-Making (PhysUnderstand), Poster
summary: Sparse-frame video-language models can change their answers when only the sampling timestamps shift. Raw agreement exposes this problem, but it need not rank errors better than token confidence or identify which additional observation will repair an answer. We argue that answer risk and action value must be estimated separately. PhaseGuard+ probes a frozen VLM at controlled temporal offsets, predicts the reliability of the phase-vote answer, and predicts the example-wise correctness gain of a specific rescue action. The second score routes only examples expected to benefit from denser frames or a stronger VLM. Both predictors use lightweight models trained on public data; the VLMs remain frozen. We use 256 Perception Test videos for method development and evaluate on a disjoint 256-video test set comprising 554 Physics questions. For Qwen3-VL-8B, reliability AUROC rises from 68.0% with token softmax to 74.8% (+6.8 pp, 95% CI [2.6, 10.7] pp). Routing 30% of questions to Qwen3-VL-32B reaches 67.87% accuracy, compared with 63.66% for budget-matched random routing (+4.21 percentage points, CI [1.89, 6.40]). All four tested rescue pairs significantly outperform random routing. Temporal sensitivity becomes actionable when the system learns both whether an answer is unreliable and whether an available action is likely to fix it.

title: Spatio-Temporal Detection of Photovoltaic Systems on Industrial Building Rooftops Using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning
summary: The global transition toward carbon-neutral energy systems is heavily dependent on the rapid deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) infrastructure, yet the speed of this expansion has outpaced the ability of administrative registries to maintain accurate records. While high-resolution commercial imagery is often used for monitoring, its high cost and infrequent updates can create an information gap for grid operators, energy infrastructure developers and policymakers. This study addresses the lack of scalable monitoring for industrial-scale rooftop PV systems by developing a machine learning framework that utilizes open-access, multispectral Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. By integrating building geometries from OpenStreetMap with Sentinel-2 reflectance data, a Random Forest model was trained to identify the specific spectral signatures of PV modules. Moving beyond theoretical modeling, this work emphasizes practical implementation through the development of an interactive web-based prototype for on-demand site monitoring. The application enables users to retrieve up-to-date satellite observations and assess the presence of PV systems on industrial building rooftops. The tool incorporates quality metrics that inform users whether a prediction is supported by sufficient training data density or requires manual verification. This end-to-end framework demonstrates that open-source medium-resolution data can effectively bridge this monitoring gap.

title: Super-resolution as Spatial Downscaling: Coherence, Structure and Task Utility in Earth Observation
comment: 41 pages, 12 figures. Code: this https URL
summary: Learned satellite super-resolution is commonly assessed by pixel fidelity and potential downlink savings, but these criteria do not establish whether the reconstructed field preserves spatial structure or supports reliable downstream analysis. We treat single-image super-resolution as a spatial downscaling problem and evaluate four lightweight networks, including our compact 0.36 million-parameter model, against interpolation using pixel metrics, directional variograms, spectral band correlation, codispersion and observation coherence. On 735 satellite tiles from 190 scenes, the networks differ by at most 0.03dB and outperform bicubic interpolation by $1.39-1.42$dB at $\times 2$. They recover about 30% of the spectral power above the observation's Nyquist frequency and, at $\times 4$, produce more isotropic fields than the reference (range anisotropy 0.59 against 0.49). Energy-based metrics can favour invented detail. Enforcing coherence reaches the quantisation limit, yet at least 99.7% of the remaining error lies in the observation operator's null space, which coherence cannot constrain. Under spatially blocked, paired evaluation with two backbones and a sharpening control, learned reconstruction changes land-use accuracy by $-1.0$ to $+3.1$ percentage points (significant in 7 of 24 comparisons) and building-change F1 by $-0.015$ to $+0.024$ (none significant) relative to bicubic interpolation, and amplifies spurious change between two observations of an unchanged scene by $1.3-1.5$ times where interpolation attenuates it. Full-resolution JPEG\,2000 matches or exceeds reduced-resolution transmission with reconstruction at every matched bitrate. Learned reconstruction is most useful when only low-resolution imagery is available, and its evaluation should combine pixel metrics with spatial structure, observation coherence and task-level tests under spatial validation.

title: REAP: Learning General Rearrangement Heuristics from Motion-Planner Feedback
summary: Robotic rearrangement tasks require planning sequences of actions that fulfill high-level specifications while also being geometrically feasible. Symbolic abstractions make the combinatorial structure of rearrangement tasks tractable, but they usually do not fully capture the geometric constraints that determine which actions a robot can actually realize. These constraints are hard to express in the symbolic model. We propose REAP (Rearrangement with Elicited Action Preconditions), a framework in which a relational graph neural network heuristic is learned over a simple symbolic abstraction. A motion planner serves as a supervisor that elicits the hidden geometric preconditions of the problem during training. Deployed with greedy best-first search, the learned heuristic generalizes out-of-distribution along object count, plan length, and object arrangement, and can be trained jointly on several domains. Compared to classical heuristic search and learning-based baselines, REAP solves more problems, requires roughly an order of magnitude fewer motion-planner queries than comparable methods, and the action it ranks first is geometrically feasible in 94% of sampled states, against 22% for a random choice.

title: How Much Can We Prune? Exploring the Performance Limits of Visual Token Pruning
summary: Visual token pruning is increasingly used to reduce the memory and inference costs of vision-language models. Existing work has largely focused on designing method-specific selectors and demonstrating incremental improvements over prior methods at selected token budgets. It remains unclear whether the resulting performance reflects an inherent limit of visual token pruning or the limitations of current token-selection algorithms. We take a complementary perspective and ask: \emph{how well can visual token pruning perform when offline search cost is not the primary constraint?} We formulate pruning for general image understanding as selecting, under a fixed budget, one shared visual-token subset that supports a broad distribution of questions about an image. We approximate this utility with a finite auxiliary QA set generated by a frontier VLM and optimize a teacher-forced answer-probability objective with the evaluated model frozen. Motivated by the conceptual monotonicity and diminishing returns of adding visual evidence, we construct nested subsets greedily and introduce \emph{QA mini-batch greedy} (QA-MBG), which estimates token marginal gains from randomly sampled QA components at each step. Empirically, QA-MBG is both cheaper and more effective than full greedy. With one frontier-VLM call and approximately $0.5$ H100 GPU-hours per image, it produces a nested subset trajectory covering keep ratios up to $0.3$. Across Qwen3-VL-4B and Gemma~4 E4B on $900$ images from nine benchmarks, we find significant headroom over evaluated pruning baselines on held-out QA and image-grounded long-form generation, while the searched subsets substantially narrow the gap to full-token inference.

title: FrameScout: Scouting Query-Relevant Frames for Long Video Understanding
summary: Long video understanding requires VideoLLMs to answer queries about videos spanning tens of minutes to hours, but such long videos produce far more visual tokens than current VideoLLMs can process. To address this issue, keyframe selectors are proposed to select the most query-relevant frames by computing the similarity between frame and query embeddings. Existing selectors either encode frames independently without temporal context or process chunks in isolation with ranking objectives that are difficult to optimize. To alleviate those limitations, we propose FrameScout with two core designs: (i) a streaming selector architecture that leverages a sliding-window KV cache and successor aggregation to produce temporally-contextualized frame embeddings; (ii) a frame-query contrastive objective that aligns frame and query embeddings in a shared space, directly training the selector to distinguish relevant frames from irrelevant ones. Extensive experiments on three long-video benchmarks and six base VideoLLMs demonstrate that FrameScout consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance. Code is available at this https URL .

title: SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are the backbone of many state-of-the-art multimodal systems, but often encode spurious and harmful associations from their training data. While prior work focuses on removing known biases from VLMs, methods for discovering unanticipated associations for retrieval tasks remain underexplored. We introduce SPELUNKA, an automated, inference-time framework for finding unanticipated distributional biases for retrieval tasks in VLMs without pre-specified labeled subgroups, inference-time human supervision, or model fine-tuning. Given a concept of interest, SPELUNKA generates captions for related images, extracts relevant entities from captions, and selects semantically meaningful associations. A frequency-based detection rule then identifies spurious associations by measuring over- or under-representation of these attributes in a VLM's top-ranked outputs relative to their full dataset distribution. We evaluate SPELUNKA across four datasets, and find that it 1) successfully recovers both synthetic and naturally occurring spurious correlations, 2) achieves an average AUROC of 0.93 across four datasets in identifying images strongly associated with a query, and 3) outperforms baselines in finding features that are strongly associated with a given query.

title: SituHOI: Scalable Capture of Scene-Situated Full-Body Human-Object Interaction
summary: Modeling human-object interaction (HOI) in real environments requires jointly representing whole-body motion, manipulated objects, and scene geometry, yet existing datasets trade off scalable capture against structured, scene-aligned supervision. We introduce SituHOI, a large-scale RGB-D dataset containing 18,429 annotated clips across 16 indoor rooms and approximately 86 hours of quality-screened activity. It pairs recordings from a single moving RGB-D camera with static scene scans, object geometry, language descriptions, and estimated human and object trajectories. Using the scans as persistent references, our pipeline combines camera localization and depth-based metric alignment with human mesh recovery, object tracking, and temporal refinement to register all geometric annotations in a shared floor-aligned frame. These data support FlexHOI-Bench, a goal-conditioned joint motion prediction benchmark with variable observation and prediction durations. Given observed histories, scene and object geometry, and a terminal object pose, models predict future human and object motion. We provide SharedHOI as a reference predictor and evaluate world-space accuracy and human-object coordination. On a MoCap subset, our pipeline reduces human G-MPJPE from 195.4 to 68.3 mm and object translation error from 43.0 to 28.7 mm. SharedHOI leads four adapted baselines on all three aggregate FlexHOI-Bench metrics. Data will be released upon acceptance. An anonymized code repository is available at this https URL .

title: Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series
summary: Video world models learn how visual environments evolve by predicting missing or future content. However, physical-state information can provide useful context for predicting how environments evolve. Prior work incorporates this information through different mechanisms: domain-specific physical laws can complicate multi-domain training, while supervision on individual frames or frame pairs gives limited attention to how physical state evolves over time. We introduce Time-JEPA, which fine-tunes a video world model using low-dimensional, temporally aligned physical time series as auxiliary supervision. Physical time series connect video representations with physical state at corresponding temporal positions, encouraging the model to preserve how physical state evolves. In multiple domains including autonomous driving, robot manipulation, and human motion, Time-JEPA improves current-state decoding, multi-horizon future-state prediction, and kinematic reconstruction over matched video-fine-tuned controls across both condition and state-variable distribution shifts. Multi-domain training provides aggregate gains over matched single-domain training in all three tasks. External evaluations further suggest that time-series supervision improves sensitivity to physical anomalies and the representation of physical interactions, including in unseen scenarios. Aggregate gains on a second video backbone indicate that the method can be applied to more backbones. These results suggest that physical time series help video world models better understand the physical world.

title: RL Teaches VLMs Where to Attend but Not How to Perceive
summary: Although reinforcement learning (RL) effectively trains Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents, the mechanisms behind these capability gains are poorly understood. Across four diverse agent environments, we investigate whether the task-success gains from multi-turn RL are accompanied by improved grounded visual question answering about the environment. To assess this, we design environment-specific grounded VQA tasks that reveal improvements in grounded visual understanding. Representational probing shows that vision-encoder probe accuracy remains relatively stable, while LLM-layer probe accuracy improves. Attention analysis further reveals that LLM layers pay more attention to visual tokens during RL training. To test whether increased attention to visual tokens contributes to VQA gains, we introduce a lightweight plug-and-play intervention using a fixed attention bias. Without updating model parameters or computing gradients, this intervention partially restores VQA gains on the untrained model. These results reveal better utilization of visual information as a key mechanism behind the gains from RL.

title: Pretrained Features as Teachers, Not States: Compact Latent World Models for Visual Planning
summary: A key design choice in visual world models is what information the latent state is encouraged to preserve. Models that learn a latent space with only a latent-prediction objective adapt to environment dynamics, but the predictive objective alone admits collapsed solutions and provides no explicit constraint on the visual information retained by the latent. Models built directly on pretrained visual features inherit a strong visual prior, but tie prediction and planning to a frozen state space. We propose Anchor-WM, which instead uses pretrained visual features as a teacher for learning a compact latent state rather than as the world-model state itself. Anchor-WM learns this compact latent with action-conditioned dynamics, while distilling the dense DINO representations through a training-only distillation head. This encourages the compact latent to retain visual information captured by the pretrained representation while discouraging representational collapse. At inference, the DINO encoder and distillation head are discarded, allowing prediction and planning to operate entirely in the learned latent space. Anchor-WM achieves the best average success rate across the four evaluated environments while enabling substantially faster planning than world models operating directly on DINO patch features. These results show that pretrained visual features can effectively guide world-model learning without defining the state space used for prediction and planning.

title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly struggle with fine-grained 3D spatial coherence and accurate structural reproduction in Blender, leaving substantial headroom for future 3D-native agentics.

title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
summary: Fine-grained visual understanding requires distinguishing subtle differences in local attributes and spatial relations, yet remains challenging for existing vision-language models. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) offer a new opportunity through generation pathways that preserve rich visual information complementary to understanding. However, existing generation-assisted understanding methods mainly rely on generative supervision or explicit generation and have not systematically explored direct use of native generation-side representations. To address this gap, we systematically analyze what generation-side representations offer for fine-grained understanding, finding that they are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes, capture task-relevant changes missed by understanding-side representations, and depend on correct spatial organization for this advantage. Guided by these findings, we design GAFU, a post-training framework that unlocks native generation-side information for fine-grained understanding. It compresses generation-side visual representations into compact \(G\) tokens that preserve fine-grained visual details, enabling task-conditioned retrieval by the understanding pathway. Experiments show that GAFU consistently outperforms SFT baselines trained on the same data across diverse visual understanding tasks and UMM architectures, with maximum relative improvements of 20.00\%, 17.94\%, and 8.62\% on VStar-Bench, OmniSpatial, and VSR-Bench, respectively. Overall, GAFU converts complementary information from the generation pathway into gains in fine-grained visual understanding, providing an effective path toward synergy between generation and understanding in UMMs.

title: Single-Pass Decision Scores Enable Rapid Classification with Adjustable Thresholds in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
comment: 29 pages (18 pages main text, 11 pages Supplementary Information), 5 figures, 3 tables
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer binary clinical questions with a yes or no token, leaving the decision threshold implicit and fixed. We derive a continuous score from a single forward pass by renormalizing the probabilities of the yes and no tokens, allowing the threshold to be adapted to clinical needs without retraining. We evaluated this approach with MedGemma and Gemma-3 (4B and 27B) on six medical imaging datasets. The default threshold was frequently misaligned with the task: for identifying normal chest radiographs, MedGemma-27B labeled every image as abnormal, whereas a validation-selected threshold yielded a sensitivity of 0.945 and a specificity of 0.696. Normalization achieved the highest AUROC on four of six datasets (CheXpert: 0.819 vs. 0.777 for raw and 0.743 for text-elicited probabilities), and a single decision required 53-79 ms on one GPU. This simple post-hoc method turns medical MLLMs into fast classifiers with adjustable operating points. Code: this https URL

title: Automatic Cause Determination in Road Scene Understanding Using Qualitative Reasoning and Four-Valued Logic
comment: Author manuscript of the paper published in the 2025 IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV)
summary: Road scene understanding in automated driving (AD) aims to build a comprehensive analysis of video sequences taken on the road by embedded or fixed cameras (e.g., mounted on vertical road signals). One goal is to identify the relevant actors in the scene and another goal is to determine the causes that have triggered a specific action of the ego car (i.e., stop, slow down, turn left, etc.). In a complex urban environment, these causes can be multiple, confusing, possibly contradictory to other causes and not easily expressible using simplistic reasoning. Still, providing accurate {\it automatic cause determination} supports a) user acceptance by providing appropriate explanations to the car passengers and road users; b) increased road safety by providing detailed road scene understanding to traffic. In this paper, we propose using spatiotemporal reasoning and Belnap's four-valued logic to formulate complex causes of AD action in a road scene. We compute these causes by analysing a Qualitative eXplainable Graph (QXG), which is an abstract representation of the road scene capturing spatiotemporal relations between road entities. Starting from a QXG, our approach called \tool, is targeted to determine complex causes of a selected AD action occurring in a specific frame of a road scene. The usefulness of \tool is demonstrated on several scenes extracted from the well-known NuScene dataset.

title: ProV-Mem: Proactive Memory for Streaming Video Question Answering
summary: Proactive streaming video question answering requires a model to continuously monitor an incoming stream and autonomously decide when to speak, what to say, and whether to emit a response. Existing streaming systems face a fundamental difficulty: retaining long visual histories is costly, whereas discarding them can lead to missed events and repeated responses. We propose \textbf{ProV-Mem}, a training-free proactive memory framework built around a frozen VLM backbone. ProV-Mem decomposes the proactive decision into three lightweight memory tiers: a temporal-trigger memory controls when to query the backbone and recovers from prolonged silence, an instructional memory guides what to say through a fixed prompting prior for concise and visually grounded generation, and an episodic memory determines whether to emit by filtering near-duplicate responses. Under an idealized conditional-sufficiency assumption, we derive a stagewise approximation bound relating the decomposed process to a full-state joint policy. We further introduce Cost-Aware Area Under the Curve (\textbf{CAUC}), which extends PAUC by explicitly discounting redundant, overly frequent, and unnecessarily long emissions. Experiments on the four scenarios of ProactiveVideoQA show that ProV-Mem achieves the best CAUC across all scenarios and the best PAUC on WEB, EGO, and TV, while maintaining low per-response inference latency.

title: Causal Spatio-Temporal Neural Distance Fields for Counterfactual Cardiac Anatomy
comment: Published at Off-Grid @ MICCAI 2026. Code: this https URL
summary: Counterfactual cardiac anatomy can support risk modelling and intervention planning, by predicting how a patient's heart would change under altered clinical conditions. However, current shape generative models are conditional on clinical variables and disregard causal links between these variables. Thus, they cannot answer counterfactual questions about how a given subject's anatomy would change under a different clinical profile. Modelling the heart's continuous movement over the cardiac cycle requires a representation that is itself continuous in space and time. Spatio-temporal neural distance fields provide this while separating clinical conditioning from subject-specific shape. We place a structural causal model (SCM) over the set of clinical variables (age, sex, smoking, BMI, heart rate, systolic blood pressure), before the condition encoding of the spatio-temporal neural distance field which represents the left atrial complex over a cardiac cycle by signed distance fields. An intervention of the clinical variables, propagated through a SCM before the 4D counterfactual, is constructed from the neural distance field. The generated counterfactuals follow dose-response under age interventions and transforms the male distribution to closely match the female distribution under the intervention $\mathrm{do(\mathrm{female}{=}1)}$. By doing inverse interventions the model also approximates the original anatomy with sub millimeter precision. To our knowledge, this is the first counterfactual generation of 4D cardiac anatomy and the first integration of an SCM with an implicit neural representation as its imaging mechanism.

title: spora: A Unified Multimodal Dataset and Platform for Spatial Proteomics
summary: Spatial proteomics (SP) captures the molecular composition and spatial organization of tissues at single-cell resolution, opening a direct view of the cellular ecosystems that drive disease. Protein panels, acquisition platforms, and tissue contexts differ from one cohort to the next, and a coherent picture of tissue biology can only emerge from models trained to bridge this heterogeneity. Foundation models offer the natural path forward, but their training depends on large, harmonized corpora that span platforms, panels, and cohorts. No public resource currently approaches that scale; available data sit in small, narrowly scoped releases with incompatible formats and conventions. We present $\texttt{spora}$, a large-scale multimodal SP dataset of 13,546 standardized multiplex images from 5,477 patients across 35 cohorts and five major SP technologies. Curated with biomedical experts, $\texttt{spora}$ provides model training-ready formats together with cell and tissue segmentations, structured clinical metadata, and, where available, paired H&E enabling the training of virtual staining models. It is complemented by $\texttt{spora [io]}$, a unified interface for tiling, sampling, and standardization across all cohorts and modalities, and $\texttt{spora [bench]}$, a benchmark suite spanning cell phenotyping, diagnostic and therapeutic prediction as well as virtual staining tasks across twelve cohorts that places current SP foundation models on common ground against task specific baselines.

title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs
summary: Native multimodal large language models (native MLLMs) jointly encode visual and linguistic sequences within a unified autoregressive Transformer, emerging as a promising paradigm for multimodal understanding. Unlike conventional ViT-based MLLMs relying on external vision encoders, ViT-free native MLLMs tokenize pixel patches directly, potentially suffering severe visual token redundancy. A pilot study confirms this: unlike ViT-based models that degrade under compression, ViT-free MLLMs tolerate aggressive compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. Yet existing compression methods target ViT-based settings, leaving native MLLMs, which stand to gain the most, unexplored. To close this gap, we introduce an analysis pipeline centered on token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy, revealing that (i) redundancy is distributed independently and heterogeneously along height and width axes, and (ii) early-layer visual tokens are indiscriminable and uniformly redundant. Guided by these findings, we propose PACE (Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs), the first visual token compression framework tailored for native MLLMs with Multimodal-RoPE. Leveraging dimensional decoupling of positional encoding, PACE decomposes attention into two orthogonal spatial saliency estimates along height and width, gated by a positional attention signal, yielding direction-aware importance with negligible overhead. It further casts token budget allocation as Pareto optimization over performance preservation, inference efficiency, and spatial coverage, jointly identifying optimal compression depths and retention ratios. Experiments show PACE maintains near-lossless performance at only 25%-50% visual token retention, even improving several benchmarks, while delivering over 2x FLOPs reduction.

title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control
summary: When a robot possesses more degrees of freedom than a task requires, multiple trajectories can achieve the same objective using distinct motion styles. Compositional robot control aims to preserve a selected style while simultaneously executing an independent task command, effectively balancing these potentially competing objectives. In this paper, we present CODES, a framework for compositional robot control that discovers a coherent style repertoire from diverse recordings and composes it with independent commands. First, motion retargeting maps the recordings to motions executable by the target robot; next, weakly supervised consensus encoding and density-based clustering identify styles within and across recordings without a prescribed count; finally, reinforcement learning trains a policy to compose the discovered styles with independent commands. We evaluate CODES on a Unitree Go2 quadruped across two simulators and physical hardware. Compared to baselines, CODES significantly improves kinematic coherence. Furthermore, our controller successfully tracks velocity commands that generalize beyond the support of the recorded data, exhibiting robust and distinguishable style characteristics during both cross-simulator and real-world hardware deployments. Project website: this https URL

title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
summary: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

title: An Anatomy-Aware Staged Pipeline for Vessel-Specific Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation in CT and MR Angiography
comment: Submitted version (7 August 2026) of a paper accepted at SWITCH+ 2026, a MICCAI 2026 workshop (TopAneu 2026 challenge track). Table 1 entries shown as dashes were pending at submission; the final version with complete results will appear in the MICCAI 2026 Satellite Events proceedings (Springer LNCS). 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table
summary: The TopAneu 2026 challenge requires intracranial aneurysms to be segmented at the voxel level and assigned to one of more than fifty vessel-specific classes, on CT and MR angiography alike. We address it with a six-stage anatomy-aware pipeline rather than a single segmentation network. A logistic-regression classifier routes each scan to a modality-specific branch; networks segment the vasculature, first as a binary mask and then over the full 36-class arterial taxonomy; a candidate localiser turns raw angiography and vessel priors into suspicious regions; a candidate-centred network segments the lesion in each crop; connected components become instances; and a per-instance classifier assigns each its anatomical location. Two principles organise the design. Whenever an upstream model output becomes a downstream training input it is generated out-of-fold, so no stage trains on unrealistically clean predictions of itself. And the anatomical decision is made once per lesion rather than once per voxel, which fits the data: of 406 connected aneurysm components in the full release, 405 carry exactly one location label. Task 1 is read off the Task 2 mask, making the two consistent by construction. We report stage-wise performance and a five-part ablation isolating what vessel priors and class-aware sampling contribute at each stage.

title: ChairNav: Cross-Embodiment Pre-training and Personalization for Long-Horizon Wheelchair Navigation
summary: Developing autonomous electric wheelchairs capable of long-horizon sidewalk navigation is critical for accessible personal mobility, yet existing approaches either focus on indoor map-based navigation or rely on expensive, complex sensor stacks to achieve full autonomy. In this work, we propose to tackle outdoor sidewalk navigation by leveraging visual navigation foundation models and large-scale navigation datasets, which offer strong generalization using lightweight hardware. To this end, we present ChairNav, a novel framework that adapts a general visual navigation model into a personalized electric wheelchair navigation system using a three-stage data pyramid. To address the scarcity of in-domain data, ChairNav first pre-trains on large-scale cross-embodiment datasets transformed into the wheelchair domain, followed by mid-training on a small number of wheelchair demonstrations to eliminate remaining domain gaps. Finally, a post-training stage refines the deployed model from user interventions to personalize its behavior. We deploy ChairNav on a commercial electric wheelchair equipped with an RGB-D camera and an onboard NVIDIA Jetson compute module. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of each stage in our data pyramid: pre-training reduces lateral ADE by 18%, and post-training increases the mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m. Further evaluation on kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes shows that our system operates autonomously for 93.4% of total driving time, demonstrating its potential for everyday accessible mobility. Demo video and more details are at this https URL .

title: CLARO: Clutter Aware Robot Orchestrator for Open-Vocabulary Grasping using VLM Agents
summary: Robots that follow natural-language instructions unlock a wide range of autonomous applications in households, warehouses, and labs. Real-world environments are diverse and often heavily cluttered, requiring robots to plan over multiple steps, act, and replan as they work toward a goal. We present CLARO (CLutter-Aware Robot Orchestrator), a VLM agent that orchestrates a set of perception and manipulation skills: open-vocabulary object detection, segmentation, 6-DoF grasping, and non-prehensile pushing to locate and retrieve a language-specified target in clutter. CLARO maintains a memory of its past actions to support long-horizon execution, and emits manipulation targets (grasp poses/3D waypoints) allowing transfer across robot arms without task-specific training. We evaluate CLARO against a range of methods on a dynamic simulation environment and standard image-based benchmarks, demonstrating strong generalization across object classes, lighting, and clutter levels. CLARO attains an average success rate of 89.1%, a relative improvement of over 16% on the strongest competing method in high cluttered scenes. We further analyze performance along grounding and grasping axes to characterize where each method succeeds and fails. Finally, we deploy CLARO on a robot arm across diverse cluttered scenes, achieving a success rate of 88.8%, and demonstrating strong sim2real generalizability.

title: DinoMUSE: A DINOv2-guided Framework for Unsupervised Lateral Motion Estimation in Ultrasound Elastography
summary: Quasi-static ultrasound elastography (USE) is a non-invasive imaging method for assessing soft tissue mechanical properties. Limited by low resolution, low sampling frequency and lack of phase information in the lateral direction, accurate lateral motion estimation remains a critical bottleneck in USE. Existing methods mainly rely on local image matching and physical constraints (such as tissue incompressibility assumption and effective Poisson's ratio), which lack sufficient contextual information. We present DinoMUSE, a DINO-guided mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework for unsupervised lateral motion estimation in USE. DinoMUSE incorporates high-level visual representations learned by DINOv2 into the motion estimation network to provide global contextual guidance. To facilitate effective interaction between DINOv2 features and local matching features, an MoE-based feature-fusion module adaptively transforms and integrates the two representations. Evaluations against NCC, GLUE, RAFT, and sPICTURE on simulation and in-vivo breast datasets show that DinoMUSE substantially improves lateral estimation accuracy while maintaining competitive axial performance. Specifically, DinoMUSE reduces the mean square error (MSE) of lateral displacement and strain estimation by 60% and 65%, respectively, compared with a SOTA algorithm on the simulation dataset. For in-vivo breast data, DinoMUSE achieves axial strain SNR and CNR of 5.70 and 4.82, and lateral strain SNR and CNR of 4.61 and 2.23, compared to 4.11 and 3.32, and 4.57 and 2.13 for the best competing method, alongside improved lesion visualization. These findings indicate the potential of leveraging transferable visual representations and adaptive feature fusion to improve lateral motion estimation in USE. The code is available at xxxxxxxx.

title: ProtoGTX: Prototype-Aligned Graph Transformer for Explainable Whole-Slide Image Analysis
comment: 14 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Code: this https URL
summary: Deep learning has achieved strong performance in computational pathology, but explaining whole-slide image (WSI) predictions remains challenging. Existing explanation methods often highlight important regions without identifying their morphological patterns, leaving a gap between patch-level computational evidence and slide-level pathological interpretation. We propose ProtoGTX, a graph-based framework that combines spatial contextualization with a flexible morphological prototype vocabulary. ProtoGTX separates the reference prototypes used to define morphological concepts from the predictive model: the reference vocabulary can be generated from training data by unsupervised clustering or supplied externally, and remains fixed during classifier training. Patch features are first contextualized over a spatial graph, after which learnable prototypes representing morphological concepts are optimized through cross-attention. Their slide-level activation profile is aligned with the morphological composition induced by the fixed reference prototype bank. On the CPTAC and BRACS datasets, ProtoGTX outperforms the evaluated MIL, prototype-based, and graph-based baselines, with particularly pronounced improvements on BRACS. Qualitative analyses further show that spatial contextualization transforms fragmented patch-level prototype assignments into more coherent tissue regions. In BRACS, prototype maps also co-localize with pathologist annotations and regions relevant to slide-level prediction. These results demonstrate that ProtoGTX provides complementary semantic and spatial explanations while retaining a prototype vocabulary that can be defined independently of the predictive model. Code is available at this https URL .

title: SynerGest: Temporal-Spatial Synergistic Gesture Generation for Dyadic Conversations
summary: Co-speech gesture generation in dyadic conversations for creating immersive virtual avatars remains highly challenging. Existing models often struggle to balance kinematic stability with rhythmic responsiveness and suffer from semantic entanglement, leading to either generic mean-pose regression or unnatural micro-jitters. To address these challenges, we propose SynerGest, a high-fidelity dyadic gesture generation framework grounded in Contrastive Flow Matching (CFM). Specifically, our CFM objective explicitly penalizes mismatched semantic pairs during training, discouraging spatial shortcuts and over-smoothed predictions while improving conditional semantic alignment. Furthermore, to overcome architectural bottlenecks, we introduce the Impulse-Trend Synergistic Attention (ITSA) module. Grounded in the key insight of decoupling "what moves" from "when it moves," ITSA models sharp, speech-driven rhythmic impulses separately from continuous kinematic trends, supporting precise audio-motion synchronization and global structural stability. Extensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations on two public datasets demonstrate that SynerGest achieves state-of-the-art performance, delivering contextually responsive and kinematically fluid dyadic interactions.

title: Implicit Neural Models for Direct Multi-Shell Diffusion MRI Signal Estimation
comment: 23 pages (9 pages main text + supplementary material), 9 figures, 18 tables
summary: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging is a noninvasive technique that is sensitive to the motion of water molecules in human tissue. The image signal is commonly described in q-space; however, a complete coverage of this space is often infeasible due to hardware and acquisition time limitations. In this work, we propose to represent the entire diffusion signal using an implicit neural representation network with wavelet activation functions. The signal space is encoded using Fourier features and spherical harmonics basis functions for a continuous output distribution of the raw diffusion data, enabling both super-resolution and q-space interpolation. Additionally, we introduce a pretraining strategy using a group template, enabling faster per-subject optimisation when combined with nonlinear registrations of subjects into template space. We tested the method with 10 subjects from the Human Connectome Project and 26 subjects from in-house data (multidimensional diffusion MRI from a Parkinson's disease cohort). The results show that the proposed method yields high-fidelity reconstructions with significantly reduced memory requirements compared to raw diffusion-weighted images. The pretraining scheme showed good generalisability properties on data acquired with very different protocols. We further assess the method on downstream metrics relevant to diffusion MRI data from the learned representations.

title: Benchmarking and Improvement of Artifact Segmentation Methods in H&E-Stained Whole Slide Imaging
summary: Technical artifacts introduced during tissue preparation or slide scanning remain a major obstacle to developing robust computational pathology algorithms for hematoxylin and eosin (HE)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs). Despite the growing number of quality-control tools, their real-world utility remains hard to assess because of the limited number of publicly available implementations and the lack of systematic, multi-dataset comparisons. This paper presents a benchmark of artifact segmentation methods for HE-stained WSIs. After a literature review, six publicly available algorithms were selected and compared in terms of their ability to segment artifact-free tissue and selected artifact classes. Two publicly available datasets and a newly introduced dataset released to support further research were used for evaluation. Tissue samples from multiple medical centers and different organs are included, enabling evaluation across heterogeneous data sources. Segmentation performance was assessed using Dice Index, pixel-level recall, and false discovery rate for artifact-free tissue segmentation. For algorithms supporting multiclass artifact segmentation, class-wise Dice Index and inter-class misclassification were evaluated. In addition to segmentation quality, processing time was assessed. Statistical analysis revealed significant differences in segmentation performance between methods. HistoKit, which incorporates a modified version of the GrandQC, was identified as the best-performing algorithm, while HistoQC was the worst. In terms of artifact types, dark spots and out of focus regions were harder to segment than others. Finally, a simple post-processing step was introduced for HistoKit, which further improved segmentation performance. The benchmark establishes a reference for evaluating and developing artifact segmentation methods for HE-stained WSIs.

title: GliomaINK: A Tumor and Anatomy Conditioned Flow Matching Framework for 3D MRI Sequence Synthesis in Glioma Patients
summary: Background: Incomplete multiparametric MR examinations limit glioma characterization and downstream AI tools. Generative models can synthesize missing MRI sequences, but anatomical structure and clinically relevant tumor features are challenging to preserve. We propose GliomaINK, an anatomy-guided conditional flow matching framework for cross-sequence 3D brain MRI synthesis. Methods: A 3D SwinUNETR predicted the conditional velocity field while an auxiliary topology-preserving loss encouraged structural consistency. The model was trained on 1,083 patients from the BraTS-AG dataset and independently tested on an in-house clinical cohort. Downstream tasks include image quality, tumor segmentation, IDH1 mutation-status prediction, and overall survival prediction. Two radiologists independently evaluated the anatomical fidelity, pathological representation, and overall image quality of the synthesized images. Results: GliomaINK exhibited the highest PSNR across all six MRI translation directions in both evaluation cohorts. In the BraTS-AG test set, the PSNR reached $25.64\pm0.55$ dB for the T2W-to-T1C synthesis, compared with $13.78\pm0.32$ dB for Pix2Pix and $18.90\pm0.53$ dB for SPADE. For downstream tumor segmentation, the method showed strong performance across tumor subregions with Dice scores reaching $0.928\pm0.014$ for edema, and $0.885\pm0.040$ for enhancing tumor. For the IDH1 mutation-status prediction, GliomaINK achieved the highest AUROC score in four of the six sequence configurations, reaching $0.827\pm0.088$. Conclusion: Anatomy-guided conditional flow matching enables high-fidelity cross-sequence glioma MRI synthesis demonstrating potential for preservation of clinically relevant information in synthesized MRI and improving downstream tasks.

title: LUMINR: Intensity-conditioned Meta-learned INRs for Accelerated Medical Image Registration
summary: Implicit neural representations (INRs) have been applied to deformable image registration, where a lightweight network maps a spatial coordinate to a deformation vector. Because an INR encodes one specific signal in its parameters, a fresh network must be optimized for every image pair at test time, which is slow. Existing methods reduce this cost by meta-learning an initialization across a population of image pairs, and condition the weights of the INR globally, so the same conditioning applies at every coordinate while the deformation field it initializes varies across the domain. We propose LUMINR, a meta-learning framework that accelerates this per-pair fitting and in which the conditioning is local instead. LUMINR uses an INR that maps a coordinate, together with local intensity and gradient features, to a deformation vector, so the conditioning varies over the domain at the resolution of the field being modelled. Its objective is to find an initialization of the INR parameters from which the network can be fine-tuned to register any unseen pair in only a few optimization iterations. We evaluate LUMINR on 3D deformable registration of brain MRI from the OASIS dataset, where local conditioning and the meta-learned initialization prove complementary: early in fitting they reach a markedly higher accuracy than either does alone. Fine-tuned from that initialization, LUMINR matches the accuracy of the same conditioned INR fit from scratch in roughly a tenth of the gradient steps and a tenth of the wall-clock time, while the deformation fields stay smooth with negligible folding.

title: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests
comment: This is a pre-MIT Press publication version, accepted for publication at TACL
summary: Recovering obscured text in palimpsests, i.e. the manuscripts where the original writing (under-text) was erased and overwritten for reuse, is vital for preserving lost information. Due to the nature of the material, such a task can be highly challenging and time-consuming. This paper presents an approach towards automated palimpsest handwritten text modeling for under-text recovery. We investigate generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models, and design a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct the under-text. The recovered text is subsequently processed by a fine-tuned, attention-based handwritten text recognition network. Furthermore, we investigate a language-guided recognition framework that leverages textual class descriptions as informative priors, enabling the text recognition model to distinguish meaningful features from noise. This is achieved by grounding task-specific descriptions, phrased in words or sentences, through visual attention maps generated by pretrained vision-language models like CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training). To facilitate future research and benchmarking, we release new datasets for synthetic palimpsests (currently scarce), CLIP-compatible text descriptions, and pre-trained models with code.

title: OrTeN: Neural Inverse Graphics for Joint Terrain and Line-scan Camera Trajectory Reconstruction
summary: Digital terrain maps (DTMs) are used for landing site selection, terrain-relative navigation, and geological analysis in planetary exploration. Existing state-of-practice reconstruction techniques for creating DTMs from satellite imagery use multi-view stereo, requiring complex pipelines for dealing with camera error, changing illumination, and images with limited disparity. This work introduces Orbital Terrain Networks (OrTeN), a DTM construction method that uses neural inverse rendering to jointly optimize a textured height map and orbital camera corrections from line-scan satellite images. OrTeN operates directly on calibrated line-scan images with pixel values expressed as radiance factor (I/F) and corrects both broad trajectory pose inconsistencies and high-frequency pointing jitter jointly with surface reconstruction during training. Surface-projected patch normalized cross-correlation (NCC) enforces consistency between observations of the same terrain, refining an initial rough reconstruction. A semi-empirical reflectance model and shadow rendering are used to fit surface appearance from multi-date imagery with differing solar illumination. OrTeN requires only calibrated line-scan images and initial camera poses and does not use any structural priors including ranging/depth measurements or initial rough DTMs. OrTeN is evaluated on four planetary imagery datasets. Aligned terrain RMSEs are 2.35 m at Jezero Crater, 2.82 m at Gale Crater, 16.18 m at Olympus Mons, and 0.43 m at McGetchin Crater.

title: BiNar: Bitstream Native Restorer for Bitstream-corrupted Image Restoration
summary: Bitstream-corrupted image restoration (BCIR) aims to reconstruct faithful images from corrupted compressed bitstreams. However, corruption occurs in bitstream-domain may lead to unpredictable error propagation and distortion amplification in pixel-domain, and even result in complete undecodability by standard decoders, posing significant challenge to existing image restoration paradigms. To address this challenge, we propose Bitstream Native Restorer (BiNar), a generative restoration framework that leverages fine-grained bitstream-native semantics to guide bitstream-corrupted image restoration. In BiNar, Bitstream Semantic Modeling (BSeM) extracts robust informative semantics and models sequential bytes directly from corrupted bitstream, enabling to generate fine-grained bitstream descriptions without relying on pixel decoding. Based on the descriptions,the Corruption-adaptive Multimodal Semantic Aggregation (CMSA) further extracts adaptive visual modal cues in decoded corrupted images and aggregates to bitstream descriptions. The multimodal aggregated fine-grained descriptions can serve as coherent restoration guidance. Finally, Blind Corruption Localization (BCoL) exploits the segmentation prior of visual foundation models to identify and locate error regions that requires recovery in corrupted images. The located error regions and the fine-grained descriptions jointly serve as visual prompt and language prompt of diffusion models image restoration, respectively. Extensive experiments under diverse bitstream corruption conditions show that BiNar outperforms all State-of-the-arts image restoration models regardless of perceptual quality or objective quality. Ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of fine-grained bitstream-native semantics in BCIR task.

title: Hierarchical and Query-Aware Visual Token Pruning for High-Resolution LVLMs
summary: High-resolution Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) preserve critical, fine-grained visual details by encoding a global thumbnail alongside multiple local crops. However, the resulting thousands of vision tokens introduce severe computational bottlenecks during Large Language Model (LLM) inference. Existing token pruning methods rely primarily on query-agnostic visual saliency, while current query-aware approaches either operate at a coarse crop-level resolution or compute token relevance too late, after vision tokens have already entered the heavy LLM layers. To address this, we propose a training-free, hierarchical token pruning framework that utilizes query guidance prior to executing any LLM blocks. Our top-down hierarchy first operates at the instance-level, dynamically scaling the vision token retention ratio of each sample based on its visual complexity. Next, at the crop-level, we distribute this sample budget across local crops using sentence-level cross-modal similarity. Finally, at the token-level, we exploit projected vision tokens alongside textual query token embeddings in the shared space to measure fine-grained alignment, applying a text-debiasing normalization to produce high-fidelity query scores. These query-guided budgets and scores are fused with local and global visual saliency metrics to select the most critical vision tokens. Extensive experiments on LLaVA-NeXT-7B demonstrate that our plug-and-play framework retains 98.0% and 94.8% of unpruned performance at 25% and 10% vision token retention, respectively. Notably, at 25% retention, our method delivers a 2.0x inference throughput speedup and even surpasses the unpruned baseline on POPE by 0.7 points.

title: Joint, Decoupled, or Agent: When Each Multimodal Alignment Paradigm Wins
summary: Jointly pretrained multimodal encoders are a common way to combine modalities, while alternatives integrate their information during downstream training or inference. When does each approach win? We compare three paradigms, instantiated with public checkpoints, across 16 paired datasets in five domains and multiple training-label budgets. JOINT trains a fusion head on frozen, jointly pretrained encoders. DECOUPLED trains a fusion head on frozen, independently pretrained encoders. AGENT gives a frozen LLM task instructions, labelled examples, available sample text, and supervised unimodal readouts. No paradigm dominates the complete 144 dataset-budget combinations: DECOUPLED wins 54, JOINT 44, and AGENT 46 by mean utility. ScienceQA, MELD, and MetMeme shift from AGENT to fusion as supervision increases. Between the fusion paradigms, JOINT leads on four of five QA datasets across all evaluated budgets, while higher unimodal 5-NN accuracy is associated with a relative shift toward DECOUPLED across eight classification datasets (Spearman $\rho=-0.67$). We test whether representation and task diagnostics predict these preferences on held-out datasets before fitting their candidate systems. A two-step cascade combines these diagnostics with task and budget metadata to select AGENT or fusion, then JOINT or DECOUPLED. Under leave-one-group-out evaluation, it selects the winner in 71.4% of cells versus 54.2% for metadata-only routing, with mean relative regret 0.028 versus 0.057. Using geometry, supervised representation diagnostics, and text-label matching together yields higher accuracy and lower regret than using any one of these sources with metadata. These results connect paradigm preferences to supervision budget, task format, and unimodal 5-NN accuracy. Target-task diagnostics thus support selecting among the three paradigms before candidate fitting.

title: BLANC: Adaptive Temporal Scheduling for Sign Language Production
summary: Sign language production (SLP) aims to synthesize expressive signing motion from written text. Modeling signing motion presents two key temporal challenges. First, fine-grained hand articulations demand higher temporal resolution than relatively slower body movements. Second, signing events unfold over variable durations, calling for adaptive temporal scheduling during generation. To address these challenges, we first introduce a Multi-Rate Vector Quantizer (MRVQ), an articulation-decoupled motion tokenizer that represents the body and both hands as separate discrete streams at distinct temporal resolutions. Building on this representation, we propose BLANC (BLock-wise Adaptive diffusioN with Articulatory Clock), a gloss-free SLP framework that generates variable-duration motion blocks causally while denoising tokens in parallel within each block.
